name: learned-rotary-matrix-binding-v1
model: CM97 complete plain two-state matrices versus CM98 learned rotary conjugation
interface: immutable object sequence to next original object; IDs are addresses only
data: unchanged original frozen35 key-value-binding generator and fingerprints; data seed1
budget_rule: fixed total component mass; initial maximum norm and every matrix/readout row absolute sum at most one
component_starts: trainable identity, random complex monomial matrices and initial phases, previous learned proposal; rotary random frequencies Gaussian(0,1); identical content RNG draws in both families
component_search: both complex initial coordinates, every observed object's four complex matrix entries, both rotary real frequencies; fixed-centre numerical perturbations at radii 2*2^(-sweep); full row radial projection; all readouts proposed from complete CE scalar contractions under row-l1 constraints
component_comparison: strict actual full-class minibatch CE improvement at feasible alpha=min(0.1,1/budget); approximate discovery without a global oracle
sampler: all original minibatch records, masks, duplicate occurrences and short tails; Random(seed+10000)
component_rng: Random(seed+20000), independent of sampler; plain consumes unused frequency initialization draws to match content starts
training: ordinary full-class CE; same feasible query centre; forward mode uses finite loss evaluations without CE or recurrent derivatives
stopping: fixed128-update diagnostic; all four endpoints sealed before any scoring; no claim that two epochs suffice for convergence
success: original primary success and separate raw/exact99; retain every original split and failure
limitations: two-state components, approximate discovery, one training seed, short recall; order witness and norm bound do not prove unseen-answer learning
